assets.title: Eyes on the Shelf
assets.alt: A fictional FPV workshop with a fully framed carbon quadcopter, goggles, camera tray and Ukrainian flag.
assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: landscape game mission background, 2:1 composition. Primary request: Reframe the existing workshop photograph slightly wider so the entire FPV quad is inside the frame, including every propeller blade with comfortable margin at the right edge. Input image: edit target; preserve its subject, room, objects, camera angle, lighting, colors, Dutch workshop atmosphere, goggles, component trays, shelves, plants, and blue-yellow cloth. Composition/framing: keep the 2:1 landscape layout and quiet gray work mat centered; move or widen the framing only as much as needed to reveal the clipped rear-right propeller tip and add a small clean margin around the whole drone. Constraints: change only the framing and the minimal newly exposed edge area; preserve the exact recognizable four-motor carbon-frame FPV drone, camera, antenna, goggles and workshop arrangement; realistic materials; no people; no readable labels; no new text; no logos; no weapons; no active flight; no watermark. Avoid: clipped drone parts, added or missing motors, duplicated propellers, deformed frame, altered workshop identity, dramatic cinematic effects, shallow crop.

derivation.changes: Proportional native resize only; no crop, repainting, palette quantization or semantic edit after the generated reframe.

review.original: Inspected the 1774x887 edit at native resolution. The FPV quad has four motors, four resting propellers, a front camera and margin around every blade. Goggles, component tray, shelves and blue-yellow cloth remain recognizable; no people or readable text.
review.selected: Inspected the exact 640x320 derivative at native size. All propeller blades remain inside the frame, the central mat remains quiet and the FPV silhouette is legible. Final human artwork review remains pending.
review.inGame: Observed in the registered Parts in Motion 03 game at 1280x720 with the standard objective, terrain, player, enemy and partial-reveal overlays. The scene stays legible at initial reveal and after a legal 3.6% capture. This is a bounded engineering observation, not final artwork approval or narrow-device review.
